concepts.title: Opening 1NT
concepts.rule: 15–17 HCP and a balanced hand (no singleton or void, at most one doubleton). A 5-card major is allowed.
concepts.meaning: {call} shows 15–17 HCP and a balanced hand.
concepts.reason: {hand} has {hcp} HCP and a {shape} shape ({longest}), so 1NT describes it best.
concepts.mistake: {wrongCall} does not describe a balanced {hcp}-point hand as well as 1NT does. With 15–17 HCP and a balanced shape, open 1NT.

concepts.title: Stayman
concepts.rule: After a 1NT opening, 2♣ asks opener for a 4-card major. Responder needs at least 8 HCP and a 4-card major.
concepts.meaning: {call} asks partner whether they hold a 4-card major.
concepts.reason: {hand} has {hcp} HCP and a {shape} shape ({longest}), enough to look for a major-suit fit.
concepts.mistake: {wrongCall} does not ask partner about majors. With 8 or more HCP and a 4-card major, bid 2♣ (Stayman) to look for a fit.

concepts.title: Answering Stayman with a major
concepts.rule: Over Stayman, opener bids a major in which they hold four or more cards: 2♥ or 2♠. With no 4-card major, opener bids 2♦.
concepts.mistake: {wrongCall} would deny a major, but you hold {longest}. Over Stayman, show your major.

concepts.title: Inviting game after Stayman
concepts.rule: After opener shows a major you also hold, raise to the three level with about 8–9 HCP to invite game. Opener bids game with a maximum and passes with a minimum.
concepts.meaning: {call} invites game with about 8–9 HCP and a fit in {suit}.
concepts.reason: {hand} has {hcp} HCP and support for {suit}, enough to invite but not to bid game.
concepts.mistake: {wrongCall} does not match your strength. With about 8–9 HCP and a fit, invite with a raise to the three level ({call}).

concepts.title: Jacoby transfer
concepts.rule: After a 1NT opening, 2♦ asks opener to bid 2♥, and 2♥ asks opener to bid 2♠. The transfer shows five or more cards in the major and lets the 1NT opener play the hand.
concepts.meaning: {call} asks partner to bid {suit}. It shows five or more cards in {suit}.
concepts.reason: {hand} has {longest}, so a transfer is the right tool.
concepts.mistake: {wrongCall} does not show a long {suit} suit. Use a transfer so the 1NT opener becomes declarer.

concepts.title: Completing a transfer
concepts.rule: When partner makes a transfer bid, bid the suit partner is showing, even with only two or three cards in it.
concepts.meaning: {call} completes the transfer by bidding {suit}, as partner asked.
concepts.reason: Partner asked you to bid {suit}. Completing the transfer is automatic.
concepts.mistake: {wrongCall} ignores the transfer. Always complete it by bidding {suit}.

concepts.title: Transfer, then game
concepts.rule: After a transfer is completed, responder with 10 or more HCP and five cards in the major bids game in that major.
concepts.meaning: {call} puts the partnership in game in {suit}.
concepts.reason: {hand} has {hcp} HCP and {longest}. Opposite a 1NT opening of 15–17, that is enough for game.
concepts.mistake: {wrongCall} stops short of game. With 10 or more HCP and a five-card major, bid game.

concepts.title: Passing in game
concepts.rule: When the partnership has reached a game contract and has no reason to look for slam, pass.
concepts.meaning: Pass ends the auction in the game contract.
concepts.reason: The auction has reached game. {hand} has {hcp} HCP and nothing to suggest going higher.
concepts.mistake: {wrongCall} bids beyond game, but nothing in your hand suggests slam. Pass.

concepts.title: Incorrect call
concepts.mistake: You bid {wrongCall}, but the lesson expected {call}.
